title: Master the QUERY Function in Google Sheets
description: Learn how to use Google Sheets' powerful QUERY function to filter, sort, and analyze data like a database.
intro: The QUERY function is Google Sheets' most powerful data analysis tool. It allows you to write SQL-like queries to manipulate your data, making it possible to filter, sort, aggregate, and transform data in ways that would require multiple functions in Excel.
prerequisites: Basic SQL knowledge is helpful but not required

sections.title: QUERY Function Basics
sections.content: The QUERY function takes a data range and a query string, returning the filtered and transformed results.

steps.name: Basic syntax
steps.text: QUERY has a simple syntax but powerful capabilities.

steps.name: Understanding the query string
steps.text: The query string uses a SQL-like syntax. Columns are referenced as Col1, Col2, Col3, etc.

tips: Headers parameter (optional): Use 1 if your data has column headers.
Column references are case-insensitive in the query string.

sections.title: Filtering Data with WHERE
sections.content: Use the WHERE clause to filter rows based on conditions.

example.result: All rows where Column A equals 'Sales'
example.explanation: Selects all columns where Column 1 (A) matches 'Sales' exactly.

tips: Use single quotes for text values, no quotes for numbers.
Multiple conditions can be combined with AND/OR.

sections.title: Sorting with ORDER BY
sections.content: Sort your results using ORDER BY with optional ASC (ascending) or DESC (descending).

example.formula: =QUERY(A1:C100, "SELECT Col1, Col3 ORDER BY Col3 DESC", 1)
example.result: Columns A and C sorted by column C in descending order
example.explanation: Selects columns 1 and 3, then sorts by column 3 from highest to lowest.

tips: ASC is the default if not specified.
You can sort by multiple columns.

sections.title: Aggregation with GROUP BY
sections.content: Use GROUP BY with aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, AVG to summarize data.

example.explanation: Groups by column 1 (category) and sums column 3 (sales) for each group.

tips: All non-aggregated columns must be in GROUP BY.
Common aggregations: SUM, COUNT, AVG, MAX, MIN.

sections.title: Combining Multiple Conditions
sections.content: Create complex queries by combining WHERE, ORDER BY, and GROUP BY.

example.formula: =QUERY(A1:C100, "SELECT Col1, SUM(Col3) WHERE Col2 >= DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY Col1 ORDER BY SUM(Col3) DESC", 1)
example.result: 2024 sales by category, sorted from highest to lowest
example.explanation: Filters for dates in 2024, groups by category, sums sales, and sorts descending.

tips: Use DATE keyword with YYYY-MM-DD format for date comparisons.
Parentheses can group conditions for complex logic.

summary: The QUERY function is Google Sheets' most versatile tool for data analysis. By learning its SQL-like syntax, you can filter, sort, aggregate, and transform data in ways that would require multiple Excel functions. Mastering QUERY will significantly boost your data analysis capabilities.
